nodes.label: silver.mapping_table (Tier 3 manual crosswalk)
nodes.rationale: Pre-existing manual crosswalk; two bugs fixed this round — it discarded the just-matched code (SELECT * EXCLUDE(...), kept only the flag) and treated annotation strings ('NE','A','ND','ver') as valid matches. Fixing both removed 54,771 false positives (2,857,766 -> 2,802,995 rows). Remains the highest-coverage tier (44% of volume) because human curation handles vocabulary divergence better than an exact hash.

nodes.label: B2: FIPE integration — Done 2026-08-24
nodes.rationale: Two roadmap modules (TCO depreciation, Preço Transacionado reference pricing) need FIPE data. match_tier existed in fato_volumes_base anticipating this but was never completed. Tiers activated (not redefined, to avoid changing meaning of 2.86M existing tier-3 rows): tier1 embedded DENATRAN code, tier2 new hash-canonical match (low yield, ~8%, since DENATRAN's versao lacks engine displacement), tier3 pre-existing manual crosswalk with 2 bugs fixed (dropped 54,771 false positives). Decided not to build an abbreviation-translation table to raise tier2 yield — real risk of silently assigning the wrong trim's price; tier3's human curation already solves this class of problem better.

nodes.label: C2: Architecture shapes for remaining roadmap modules
nodes.rationale: Recorded ahead of implementation so shape is agreed rather than discovered mid-build: Preço Transacionado needs its own vehicle-key mapping (third-party Nota Fiscal data, same class of problem as FIPE); Itens de Especificações is a genuine SCD Type 2 candidate (real effective-dated history, unlike dim_veiculo_atual's Type 1); TCO is a calculation engine over rate-table inputs, not a file-ingest domain; Incentivos Comerciais is campaign-grain, sourced via LLM extraction over unstructured documents plus human audit — the most architecturally novel of the six modules.
nodes.norm_label: c2: architecture shapes for remaining roadmap modules

nodes.label: SCD Type 2 considered and rejected for vehicle dims
nodes.rationale: vehicle_key alone doesn't determine segmentacao_atualizada/segmentacao_original/tipo_veiculo_principal — DENATRAN reclassifies the same model over time (~6.5% of vehicle_keys have more than one observed combination). Only data_emplacamento (sale date) exists, not a true classification-effective date, so a reliable timeline of 'when classification changed' can't be built. SCD Type 2 was considered and dropped for this reason after an external review flagged the problem.
nodes.norm_label: scd type 2 considered and rejected for vehicle dims

nodes.label: categoria_empresa (CNAE classification)
nodes.rationale: Classifies by CNAE: 45xx = concessionaria/comercio de veiculos (54% of CNPJ-invoiced volume), 771x = locadora (deliberately narrower than the full 77xx group, which would also sweep in unrelated equipment rental CNAEs).

nodes.label: empresa_key (sentinel keys -1/-2)
nodes.rationale: Two sentinels live in empresa_key rather than cnpj_basico because '00000000' is a real CNPJ (Banco do Brasil) and can't become a sentinel: -1 = sale not invoiced by CNPJ, -2 = real CNPJ with no match in any Empresas source.

nodes.label: B1: Locadoras module (CNPJ join + CNAE) — Done 2026-08-20
nodes.rationale: Not a new data source, a join against Bronze CNPJ data already on hand. Shipped gold.dim_empresa scoped to ~8,455 CNPJs observed in silver.veiculos, using two zero-overlap reference tables (bronze_master_cnpj + newly-found main.CNPJ_empresas_final) covering 99.98% together vs ~75% from either alone.

nodes.label: A1: Replace hardcoded Gold assertion with a real test suite
nodes.rationale: gold/build_volumes.py had one correctness check: assert total == 10_658_607, guaranteed to fail on any new upload since the total legitimately changes. Decision: five pytest tests mirroring silver/tests/ — volume conservation, no row loss/duplication in the fact join, build determinism (build twice, EXCEPT diff dimensions), surrogate key uniqueness, referential completeness. Gold is the most user-visible layer yet was the least tested.
nodes.norm_label: a1: replace hardcoded gold assertion with a real test suite

nodes.label: A3: Wire the test suite into CI
nodes.rationale: No CI exists at all, not even for the existing silver/tests/ suite. A test suite nobody runs automatically only catches bugs the one developer remembers to run it against.
nodes.norm_label: a3: wire the test suite into ci

nodes.label: C1: Split build_volumes.py into one build per fact table
nodes.rationale: Today one script rebuilds everything on every upload — fine with one fact table, but once Preço Transacionado/Especificações exist, an unrelated product's monthly file would trigger a full rebuild of unrelated tables. Decision: refactor into one build function per fact table sharing conformed dimensions via vehicle_key (Kimball bus architecture), done before the second product domain lands since retrofitting after is real rework.
nodes.norm_label: c1: split build_volumes.py into one build per fact table

nodes.label: Overall architecture rating: 7/10
nodes.rationale: The Emplacamentos pipeline shows real production instincts (dedup-by-hash logged before the risky step, non-fatal S3 handling, grain documented in the database itself, a deliberate SCD-2 rejection rather than cargo-culted). What holds it back: zero tests outside Silver until this review, no CI, two of six roadmap modules need architecture that doesn't exist yet, and a single-developer bus factor.

nodes.label: SQL macro over Python UDF for MotherDuck writes
nodes.rationale: create_function-based Python UDFs don't survive MotherDuck's hybrid execution — a query writing to a remote table loses the reference to the Python function mid-way. Pure SQL macros don't have this problem. General lesson: any logic that needs to run on a MotherDuck write must be pure SQL, not a Python UDF.
nodes.norm_label: sql macro over python udf for motherduck writes

nodes.label: gold.fato_volumes (view)
nodes.rationale: Kept as a view joining fact+dimensions back into the old flat shape (plus segmentacao_klume) because Vanna's training examples are calibrated against that flat format — LLMs generate GROUP BY far more reliably than JOIN. BI tools (Tableau/Power BI) connect to the physical tables instead.

nodes.label: D1: Auth / leaving Streamlit free tier — deferred
nodes.rationale: Stay on the free tier without auth for now — single/few-user prototype stage, customer data intake is human-mediated so nobody external touches the app regardless of auth state. Revisit trigger: before anyone outside the team needs to log in directly.
nodes.norm_label: d1: auth / leaving streamlit free tier — deferred

nodes.label: app.upload_log
nodes.rationale: Added after a 1958 test upload left 30 orphan rows in Bronze (AWS secret not configured on Streamlit Cloud broke the S3 step after the MotherDuck INSERT already ran). Hash is recorded right after the MotherDuck INSERT succeeds, before S3 is attempted, so an S3 failure doesn't leave a re-run vulnerable to duplicating rows.

nodes.label: A2: Lock down Vanna's database access
nodes.rationale: Vanna executes LLM-generated SQL directly against MotherDuck with no validation, allowlist, or role separation. Decision: two MotherDuck roles — a write role for the upload pipeline only, a read-only role (no DDL/DELETE) for Vanna. DB-level enforcement removes a whole class of risk more cheaply than parsing/validating generated SQL at the app level.
nodes.norm_label: a2: lock down vanna's database access

nodes.label: D2: Automating customer data intake — deferred
nodes.rationale: Keep the current pattern (customer emails a file, a human uploads via the existing page) rather than building automated inbox parsing now. Revisit trigger: when manual intake volume/frequency itself becomes the bottleneck, not before.
nodes.norm_label: d2: automating customer data intake — deferred

nodes.label: Upload schema validation
nodes.rationale: Rejects a file before any insert if a required column is missing (Data de Emplacamento, Marca, Modelo, Quantidade) or if fewer than 50% of columns match the reference DENATRAN format (staging.bronze_2024). Previously a missing column silently became NULL with no check that the file was even the right format.

nodes.label: MCP for external clients (planned)
nodes.rationale: External (paying customer) access needs fixed MCP tools (get_datamart(nome, filtros)) rather than free SQL, to structurally enforce paid-plan separation (e.g. current vs historical FIPE price) instead of scattered query policy.

nodes.label: Original gold.fato_volumes (wide OBT, deprecated)
nodes.rationale: First version was one denormalized table (marca, modelo, segmentacao_atualizada etc. repeated as text across ~7.7M rows). Reformulated to a real star schema because there was no sensible place to document columns, and Tableau/Power BI perform poorly joining on 64-bit hash keys.
